newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat stabilises after EU export award.
newsitem.headline: French wheat stabilises after EU export award.

text.p: French wheat prices halted their decline on Friday, a day after the European Union made its largest wheat export award of the season at its weekly auction.
Wheat into Rouen for October-December delivery was bid at 860 francs per tonne and offered at 865 francs, unchanged from Thursday but down 10 francs on the week.
On Thursday the EU agreed the export of 332,500 tonnes of soft wheat from the open market at a refund of 6.90 Ecus per tonne.
But dealers said they were unimpressed in the face of ample wheat supplies in the EU and fierce competition on world markets from other suppliers, particularly Argentina.
"This is just preventing wheat prices from falling. That's all," one said.
Wheat futures volume on MATIF was a thin 25 lots at mid-afternoon, with the November 1996 expiry quoted at 850 francs, down five francs on Thursday.
Maize prices were steady as rain continued to slow down the pace of the harvest, with October-December delivery into Bordeaux quoted at 880 francs.
